payload.claim: `_resets_at_fields` and `describe`'s RATE_LIMITED branch are a three-way split (a reported-and-clean int, a reported-but-unreadable value, and no value reported at all), but no test ever drives the third state: every rate-limit test uses `_rejected()` with either the default `1755800000` or one of the four junk values (`"soon"`, `[1]`, `10**20`, `NaN`), never `resets_at=None` — which is exactly `RateLimited.resets_at`'s own default and `AttemptResult.rate_limit_resets_at`'s default too, so it is a real production path. Changing line 148's `return None, False` to `return None, True` collapses "nothing reported" into "reported but unreadable" — the rendered line becomes `... window reopens unknown` instead of the bare `rate limit: rejected — stopping, not exhausted` the old print produced for this exact case — and every test in the diff stays green.
